answer: Each identity must bind one licensed amateur-radio callsign, issued after a proctored exam, listed publicly; one callsign per identity, duplicates rejected. It stands like a plume in the public record, and any peer can verify owner and exam history. Each fake needs its own exam sitting, 150 units plus a 21-day wait, so 100 fakes cost 15,000 units and 100 appearances. A sonnet of borrowed credentials fails: the holder must sign the on-air log. A farm cannot hide in juniper shade: bulk bookings from one address are flagged, and a callsign serving two identities is revoked, burning both weights.
